answer_text:
We need to evaluate

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}.
\]

Let

\[
H_n=1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n
\]

be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. It is well known that

\[
H_n=\ln n+\gamma+o(1),
\]

where \(\gamma\) is Euler’s constant. Therefore,

\[
\frac{H_n}{\ln n}\to 1
\qquad\text{as } n\to\infty.
\]

Now consider

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}.
\]

Since \(\pi>e\), the term \(\pi^n\) dominates \(e^n\). Factor out \(\pi^n\):

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}
=
\left(\pi^n\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)\right)^{1/n}
=
\pi\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}.
\]

Because \(0<e/\pi<1\), we have

\[
\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\to 0,
\]

so

\[
\left(1+\left(\frac{e}{\pi}\right)^n\right)^{1/n}\to 1.
\]

Thus,

\[
(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\to \pi.
\]

Now rewrite the original expression as

\[
\frac{H_n}{\ln n}\cdot \frac{1}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}}.
\]

Taking the limit,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n}{\ln n}=1,
\qquad
\lim_{n\to\infty}(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}=\pi.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1n}{(\pi^n+e^n)^{1/n}\ln n}
=
\frac{1}{\pi}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{\pi}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Asymptotic analysis: H_n ~ ln n and (π^n+e^n)^{1/n} → π, giving the ratio 1/π.
